pr_body: This commit introduces versioning for DAGs. Changes: - Introduced DagVersion model to handle versioning of DAGs. - Added version_name field to DAG for use in tracking the dagversion by users - Modified DAG execution logic to reference dag_version_id instead of the dag_hash to ensure DAG runs are linked to specific versions. The table relations: The versioning is based on the serialized dict changing. If a dag's serialized dict changes, a new serialized dag will be registered based on the hash diference, and consequently, a new dag version and dag code. The link from dag_version to TI is because of TaskInstance clearing. It helps us retain the previous dag version the task ran with. Closes: #42333, #42334, #42336

issue_context.title: Calculate and track DAG version
issue_context.body:
### Body

We need to calculate the DAG version based on the serialized DAG, and start tracking it on the task instance try level.

### Committer

- [x] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.

review_comments: This code smells to be non-thread safe. If multiple instances run concurrently it could generate a clash in app logic for ID generation. If this should represent an auto-increment... this should be rather pushed-down to database engine (e.g. identity column)
I will look into this
I'm using a lock on this row. That should help avoid the clash? WDYT?
Is the version number just for ordering? I wonder if we actually need it since each version already has a name as a UI identifier. We could just order by `created_at` instead.

It's not just for ordering. The version number helps to track the version changes. If a version named `my_version` is added, it first gets `my_version_1`, if there's a change in the code but the version name is still not change,  then the number will increment and we have `my_version_2`. So it's not just for ordering

one option is you could do optimistic concurrency control. 

```
update blah
set some-stuff=other-stuff, version_number=N+1
where something-something AND version_number=N
```
if no rows updated, you know something else beat you to it.

oh you have many versions... 

in that case i wonder if there might be race condition where you might lock the latest row, but then something else inserts _another_ row?
There's now a unique constraint between a dag_id and the version_number which solves the case of collision. What do you think?
why binary false?

By default, sqlalchemy-utils UUIDType uses binary for DBs that don't support UUID e.g sqlite. With binary False, it will use Char 32 to store the generated UUID: https://github.com/kvesteri/sqlalchemy-utils/blob/baf53cd1a3e779fc127010543fed53cf4a97fe16/sqlalchemy_utils/types/uuid.py#L40
could you do binary for non-sqlite?  isn't binary much more desirable where supported?
Paging @kaxil - I know you've been looking at UUID stuff recently. Any input/thoughts here?

added comment here: https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/42913/files#r1823527044

tldr: Only Postgres supports native UUIDs.
IIUC this parameter does not matter on a database that _does_ support native UUID. The question here therefore is whether we want to store the UUID as a string or binary blob on non-Postgres.

>The question here therefore is whether we want to store the UUID as a string or binary blob on non-Postgres.

Store it as string for non-Postgres dbs -- which @ephraimbuddy has already done with `binary=False` arg here.

We have a naming convention that applies the naming automatically. We no longer need to specify a name for the ORM. We should for the migration files: https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/dc91d07e298e5347ad77af25eb3533a13c71a883/airflow/models/base.py#L36
